# TDPdf v1.29.2.0

**Two "there's a workaround" answers from the last round of feedback have been replaced with actual fixes.**

## Rotate is on the toolbar

It was always reachable — right-click a page thumbnail in the Pages panel — but that's not where anyone goes looking for it first, and someone did exactly that and reported it missing. It's now a toolbar button next to Move Up/Move Down: left-click rotates the selected page(s) clockwise, right-click opens the same clockwise / counter-clockwise / fine-Transform menu the page thumbnail's right-click menu already offered.

## Taskbar previews show the right window

Open several TDPdf windows and hover the taskbar icon, and every window used to show the same blank, generic preview instead of its own content — indistinguishable from "only the active window has a preview." The cause: TDPdf's default custom title bar renders as a layered window, and Windows' compositor (DWM) can't generate a live thumbnail for a layered window on its own.

Previous advice was to turn on **Settings → "Use native window frame"** to work around it. That setting still works exactly as before, but it shouldn't have to be the answer — a default that's broken until someone finds an unrelated-sounding toggle is still a broken default. TDPdf now supplies DWM with its own rendered bitmap on request (the sanctioned mechanism other apps with custom title bars use for exactly this), so hovering the taskbar icon — or invoking Aero Peek — shows each window's actual content, with the default chrome, no setting required.
